**Area:** [Identity & security](../COVERAGE.md#security) · **Apple:** [Security](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security) · **Issues:** [`area:security`](https://github.com/kolabs-dev/isim/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%3Asecurity)

## How isim implements it

- **Keychain, adapted:** JSON files (mode 0600) per access group in `$ISIM_DATA/Library/Keychains`.
- **Keys, certificates and trust, passthrough:** the host's OpenSSL (`isim/runtime/host_pki.c`), with Apple's trust rules applied by isim.
- **CommonCrypto, passthrough:** the host's OpenSSL.

## API

| API / feature | Status | iOS | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Keychain passwords (`SecItemAdd/CopyMatching/Update/Delete`, generic + internet passwords), from Swift, C and Objective-C | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: iOS attribute keys, duplicate detection, return data/attributes/persistent refs, match limits, access groups (default: bundle id). Stored per access group in `$ISIM_DATA/Library/Keychains` (0600 JSON, not encrypted; survives app deletion, erased by `isim reset`). C and Objective-C (`<Security/Security.h>`): the same functions and items (`@_cdecl` over the Swift keychain), the `kSec…` constants with the same values, `SecCopyErrorMessageString`. Tested: SecurityTest, HelloKeychainObjC |
| Keychain access control (`SecAccessControlCreateWithFlags`, `kSecAttrAccessControl` on password items; `kSecUseOperationPrompt`, `kSecUseAuthenticationUI` Fail / Skip, `kSecUseAuthenticationContext`), from Swift, C and Objective-C | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: reading the data of an item whose flags ask for the device owner (`userPresence`, `biometryAny`, `biometryCurrentSet`, `devicePasscode`) shows LocalAuthentication's Face ID / Touch ID prompt (passcode allowed unless biometry only), once per query; a refused or cancelled prompt returns `errSecUserCanceled`; attributes need no authentication; Fail returns `errSecInteractionNotAllowed`, Skip leaves the item out. Not yet: a change of enrolled biometry does not invalidate `biometryCurrentSet` items, updates are not authenticated. Tested: HelloKeychainObjC |
| Keychain keys, certificates, identities (`kSecClassKey` / `Certificate` / `Identity`, `kSecValueRef`, `kSecReturnRef`, `kSecAttrIsPermanent`) | ✅ | ≤17 | same store as passwords; Apple's primary keys (duplicates detected), tag/label/issuer/serial queries; identities keep their private key with the certificate. Tested: SecurityTest |
| CommonCrypto (`CC_SHA*`, `CC_MD5`, `CCHmac`, `CCCrypt`/`CCCryptor`, `CCKeyDerivationPBKDF`, `CCRandomGenerateBytes`) | ✅ | ≤17 | in libSystem like iOS; contexts copyable; AES (ECB/CBC/CTR/CFB/OFB) and 3DES via the host's OpenSSL, other ciphers `kCCUnimplemented`. Known-answer tests |
| Security: `SecRandomCopyBytes`, `SecCopyErrorMessageString` | ✅ | ≤17 | |
| Security: `SecKey` (RSA 1024-8192, EC P-256/384/521: create, import/export in Apple's formats, sign/verify incl. PSS and RFC 4754, RSA PKCS#1/OAEP encryption, ECDH + X9.63 KDF, attributes) | ✅ | ≤17 | host OpenSSL; `kSecAttrTokenIDSecureEnclave` P-256 keys in the simulated Secure Enclave (not exportable, keychain items with `kSecAttrTokenID`, `kSecAttrAccessControl` asks for Face ID on use, `kSecUseAuthenticationContext`); ECIES algorithms unsupported. Tested: SecurityTest (interoperates with CryptoKit) |
| Security: certificates and trust (`SecCertificate`, `SecPolicy`, `SecTrust` create/anchors/verify date/evaluate (sync, async), chain, exceptions, revocation (`SecPolicyCreateRevocation`, `SecTrustSetOCSPResponse`, `SecTrustSetNetworkFetchAllowed`), `SecTrustSetSignedCertificateTimestamps`, `SecPKCS12Import`, `SecIdentity`) | ✅ | ≤17 | chain building on the host's OpenSSL, then Apple's rules (adapted): SSL policies need RSA ≥ 2048 bits, no SHA-1, the host in subjectAltName, the serverAuth EKU and ≤ 825 days (issued from July 2019), and, for chains to a system root (not a self-signed certificate trusted directly), ≤ 398 days (from September 2020) and Certificate Transparency (2 SCTs, embedded or given; counted, not checked against CT logs); OCSP revocation from stapled responses or the certificate's responder (`errSecCertificateRevoked`, soft-fail unless `kSecRevocationRequirePositiveResponse`: `errSecIncompleteCertRevocationCheck`); no CRL fetching. System anchors are the host's CA store, not Apple's. A URLSession challenge's trust holds the server's certificate chain (pinning; see Authentication challenges); `URLCredential(identity:certificates:persistence:)` for client certificates. Tested: SecurityTest (test CA, wildcard host, expired, self-signed, a certificate breaking each rule, OCSP good/revoked stapled and from a local responder, wrong password) |
| Certificates, policies, trust and identities from C and Objective-C (`SecCertificateCreateWithData` / `CopyData` / `CopySubjectSummary` / `CopyCommonName` / `CopyKey` / `CopySerialNumberData`, `SecPolicyCreateSSL` / `CreateBasicX509`, `SecTrustCreateWithCertificates` / `SetPolicies` / `SetAnchorCertificates(Only)` / `SetVerifyDate` / `EvaluateWithError` / `Evaluate` / `GetTrustResult` / `CopyCertificateChain` / `CopyKey` / `CopyExceptions` / `SetExceptions`, `SecIdentityCopyCertificate` / `CopyPrivateKey`, `SecPKCS12Import`, the `…GetTypeID` functions) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: `@_cdecl` functions over the Swift implementation (the row above), so C and Swift share the objects; `CFGetTypeID` answers each type's ID. Tested (SecurityCTest, on tests/security's PKI) |
| Shared web credentials (`SecAddSharedWebCredential`, `SecRequestSharedWebCredential`, `SecCreateSharedWebCredentialPassword`, `kSecSharedPassword`), from Swift, C and Objective-C | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: the credentials are the device's Passwords store (`Library/Passwords/passwords.plist`, the one AutoFill and Settings > Passwords use; no iCloud Keychain) for the app's `webcredentials:` associated domains, each confirmed by the domain's apple-app-site-association `webcredentials.apps` (`Library/isim/AASA/<domain>.json` or the network; offline: allowed, logged). Saving, updating and deleting (nil password) ask the user ("Save / Update / Delete Password?"); a request shows the saved accounts to choose from. Errors: `errSecMissingEntitlement` (not a verified domain), `errSecUserCanceled`, `errSecItemNotFound`. The passwords are `xxx-xxx-xxx-xxx` (proposed: Apple's documented format). Tested: test_vault.py (HelloVault), test_keychain_objc.py (HelloKeychainObjC) |
| Types not yet in isim (iOS 17 and earlier) | ❌ | ≤17 | not implemented, found by the 2026-10 sweep: `OS_sec_certificate`, `OS_sec_identity`, `OS_sec_object`, `OS_sec_protocol_metadata`, `OS_sec_protocol_options`, `OS_sec_trust`, `SecAsn1Template_struct`, `SecKeyKeyExchangeParameter`, `SSLCiphersuiteGroup`, `SSLProtocol`, `tls_ciphersuite_group_t`, `tls_ciphersuite_t` (12 types; with their members under "Not yet in isim") |
| `tls_protocol_version_t` in isim's Network module | 🟡 | ≤17 | adapted: implemented, but declared in isim's Network overlay instead of Security (Apple's module), so code that imports only Security does not see it; the 2026-10 sweep counts it missing from Security |
